boards.title: Your First Weekend at Michigan Technological University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to campus, finding recreation, and ending with a cultural stop in Houghton.

cards.title: 1. Mark your arrival at the east entry sign
cards.subtitle: East campus entry · Michigan Tech
cards.notes: Start with a quick arrival photo, then use the interactive campus map to identify your residence, academic buildings, and the routes between them.
cards.short_summary: A simple first landmark before you begin navigating campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech's visitor guide specifically identifies the east and west campus-entry Michigan Tech signs as photo stops.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; use the university map to plan the next stop.

cards.title: 2. Find the Husky Statue
cards.subtitle: Michigan Tech campus · Houghton
cards.notes: Make this a short orientation pause: take a photo if you like, then compare nearby building names with the campus map before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark for a first walk across Tech.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech's visitor guide lists taking a selfie with the Husky Statue among its year-round activities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; confirm its current map position before heading over.

cards.title: 3. Get your bearings at the Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union Building (MUB) · 1400 Townsend Drive
cards.notes: Walk through the first floor to spot the Campus Bookstore and student organization offices, then check posted information for campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A central gathering building with student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: The MUB is a student gathering space; its first floor includes the Campus Bookstore and student organization offices.
cards.access_notes: Check building access and individual office availability when you arrive.

cards.entity_name: J. Robert Van Pelt and John and Ruanne Opie Library
cards.title: 4. Make the library your reset point
cards.subtitle: Opie Library · heart of campus
cards.notes: Use a quiet break to locate service desks and study areas; save the library site for help with research, printing, and future coursework.
cards.short_summary: A campus resource hub for information, study, and assistance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Van Pelt and Opie Library describes its mission as creating connections in the heart of campus and promises access to information and resources.
cards.source_title: Mission, Vision, Values, and Strategy | Van Pelt and Opie Library
cards.access_notes: Verify current building hours and service availability on the library website.

cards.title: 5. See the A. E. Seaman Mineral Museum
cards.subtitle: Minerals and Materials Engineering building · Michigan Tech
cards.notes: Plan a self-paced gallery visit and look for the Michigan-mineral displays; confirm visitor access and any admission details before you go.
cards.short_summary: A named campus museum with a substantial mineral collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech's self-guided tour describes the A. E. Seaman Mineral Museum as Michigan's official mineral museum, with more than 4,000 specimens on display.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current museum hours, visitor access, and admission before arrival.

cards.title: 6. Tour the Student Development Complex
cards.subtitle: SDC · 1400 Townsend Drive
cards.notes: Stop by the recreation desk to learn which facilities fit your routine, such as the track, climbing wall, pool, courts, or ice arena.
cards.short_summary: A large recreation complex that introduces several campus activities at once.
cards.evidence_claim: The SDC includes the MacInnes Student Ice Arena, indoor track, climbing wall, pools, courts, and other recreation facilities; students have access through student fees.
cards.access_notes: Bring your student ID and check current facility rules, hours, and any reservation requirements.

cards.title: 7. Reserve a court at Gates
cards.subtitle: Gates Tennis Center · Michigan Tech campus
cards.notes: If you want an active break, reserve tennis or pickleball space ahead when possible and bring your Michigan Tech student ID to check in.
cards.short_summary: An indoor court option for a structured weekend activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Gates Tennis Center has four indoor courts, and Michigan Tech students play there free all year through Experience Tech.
cards.access_notes: Student access requires current eligibility; advance reservations may be needed.

cards.title: 8. Take a daylight loop on Tech Trails
cards.subtitle: Recreational Forest beside campus · across from the SDC
cards.notes: Choose a route appropriate to conditions and daylight, then hike, run, bike, snowshoe, or ski only with suitable gear and a checked trail plan.
cards.short_summary: A near-campus recreation system for an outdoor reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech's adjacent recreational forest features Tech Trails for Nordic skiing, snowshoeing, hiking, running, and mountain biking.
cards.access_notes: Check trail conditions, permitted uses, weather, and any current pass requirements before setting out.

cards.title: 9. Walk or roll the waterfront trail
cards.subtitle: Houghton waterfront · near Michigan Tech
cards.notes: Head out in daylight for a paved waterfront walk, jog, or bike ride; choose a turnaround point that leaves ample time to return comfortably.
cards.short_summary: A barrier-free paved route along Houghton's waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Houghton describes the Waterfront Trail as a 4.5-mile paved, barrier-free trail for walkers, joggers, and bicyclists.
cards.access_notes: Use daylight and check local conditions; the city page identifies endpoints at Waterfront Recreation and Nara Nature Park.

cards.entity_name: Rozsa Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: 10. End with the Rozsa calendar
cards.subtitle: Rozsa Center · 1400 Townsend Drive
cards.notes: Check the current program, note any ticket or content guidance, and choose a performance, gallery, or future event that works with your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus performing-arts venue with a public events calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rozsa Center hosts events by local organizations, Michigan Tech, and its Presenting Series, and publishes an upcoming-events calendar.
cards.access_notes: Check the event page for date, ticketing, age suitability, accessibility, and arrival details.
